advice: Propose one experiment on the active `sera_libxsmm_panel32` path: inside `gemm`, pack B into sixteen 32-column panels, each stored as `packed_b[p*65536 + k*32 + c] = B[k*512 + p*32 + c]`. Update the panel32 consumer to select the matching packed panel and advance 128 bytes per K step, while preserving all FP32 values and each output’s K update order. Keep allocation and packing in the timed call, with the existing ABI and general-size fallback. This is distinct from the supplied packed-B experiment on the inactive full512 path. Hypothesis: shorter, contiguous K-step addresses may improve the active consumer enough to offset packing and allocation costs. The effect is unverified.
risks: Packing adds a 1 MiB allocation and reads and writes all of B, which may outweigh any consumer benefit. Verify panel selection, bounds, pointer resets, complete C coverage, ABI and stack state, input preservation, fallback behavior, and all 48 public cases at tolerance 0.002. Then collect ten validation reports and ten alternating paired controls with power settings unchanged; apply the existing promotion and holdout gates. Do not infer a gain from isolated load behavior or noisy scores.
